about: Tally's Sorting Game - the placement strand lock (spec section 4). Four independent staircases over half-grade rungs K.0 to 8.0 (17 rungs). CCSS-M has no half-grades: rung X.0 samples the end of the previous grade / the start of grade X, rung X.5 samples grade X's first clusters. Rungs are curriculum-order judgements by the course writers (spec section 4.3), refined by item data after launch - never presented as grades the test certifies. LOCK STATUS: rungs K.0-5.5 are LOCKED at cluster level for all four strands (every cluster named here exists in standards.json clusters) - item templates may be tagged to them now. Rungs 6.0-8.0 are DEFERRED to the Pro phase lock: their cluster headings live in standards.json deferredClusters for orientation and may NOT be used as item tags yet. The K.0-2.5 rung CONTENT below is locked, and since the Launchpad tier opened (2026-11-13) those rungs route a learner into the Launchpad units through crosswalk.entryProfiles (launchpad-<unit>.1). The Launchpad audio item FORM is the short form the game already plays for a named grade of K-2 (three strands, at most four questions each, every item audio-first); a purpose-built K-2 item form (picture-only answers, no typed answers) is still to come. Chance before grade 6 has no CCSS home (SP begins at grade 6): Data & Chance rungs below 6.0 tag data clusters only, plus a plainly flagged enrichment note for chance language (spec sections 2.1/2.5 note 8).

crosswalk.about: Strand confirmed rungs combine into ONE start node (spec section 4.4): the earliest unit the learner has not yet shown the entry profile for; ties and near-misses resolve to the LOWER unit (start where success is likely, then move fast). Units before the start node are shown explored - playable and lap-eligible - never 'skipped' or 'mastered'. The Sorting Game routes; only unit test-out (5 items at unit depth) demonstrates a unit. Phase 2 (2026-11-05): the walk now covers all seven built workshops, and a run that meets every profile lands on the finale door (Explorer 7.4, the Vault of Measures) instead of past the street.
crosswalk.launchpadProfiles: LAUNCHPAD ENTRY PROFILES (locked 2026-11-13, with the tier's opening). Read like Explorer's: a profile that is fully met means the walk moves past that unit; the first unit whose profile is not met is the start. Each profile asks, per strand, the rung whose locked clusters show the bulk of what the unit teaches, and is monotone per strand. Evidence, unit by unit (unit standards from units.json, rung clusters from this file): Unit 1 The Counting Patch (K.CC.A/B/C, K.NBT.A) = Number K.5. Unit 2 The Joining Pond (K.OA.A, then facts to 20) = Algebra 1.0 (K.OA.A is rungs K.0/K.5; rung 1.0 samples adding and taking away within 20 in 1.OA.A/B). Unit 3 The Tens Trellis (1.NBT.A/B/C) = Number 1.5. Unit 4 The Balance Bridge (1.OA.D, 1.OA.A, 2.OA.A, 2.OA.C) = Algebra 2.0; its last step alone (2.OA.C, equal groups) sits at rung 2.5, which is Explorer's line, so it is not asked here and the walk keeps a separate landing for a learner at rung 2.0. Unit 5 The Hundreds Hedge (2.NBT.A, 2.NBT.B) = Number 2.5. Unit 6 The Shape Shed (K.G, 1.G.A, 2.G.A) = Shape & Measure 2.0. Unit 7 The Measuring Meadow (1.MD.A/B, 2.MD.A/C in Shape & Measure; K.MD.B, 1.MD.C, 2.MD.D in Data & Chance) = Shape & Measure 2.5 and Data & Chance 2.0. A strand a unit does not teach keeps the rung the earlier units asked (0 where none did). No Launchpad profile asks more than Explorer's first door (2.5). The short Launchpad form of the game has no Algebra staircase: its Number rung speaks for Algebra, so on that form the Algebra column reads as a second Number requirement. These are curriculum-order judgements by the course writers, like every rung here, to be refined by item data; they certify nothing.
crosswalk.rule: Walk the units in order (Explorer 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7). The start node is the first unit whose entryProfile is NOT fully met by the four confirmed rungs; a near-miss counts as not met, so ties resolve to the lower unit. If every one of the seven profiles is met, the start node is the finale door, Explorer 7.4 (the Vault of Measures): the learner has shown the entry profile for every workshop, so the street's last door is where they start, and every workshop behind them stays open for games, laps and test-out. If any confirmed rung is below 2.5, the start node sits in the Launchpad tier (open since 2026-11-13): walk the Launchpad units in order (1 to 7) the same way. Below the first Launchpad profile the start is the tier's first step, Launchpad 0.1 (Meet Tally in the Gardens); otherwise it is the door of the first Launchpad unit whose profile is NOT fully met, ties resolving to the lower unit; if all seven Launchpad profiles are met while a rung is still below 2.5, the start is Explorer 0.1 (Welcome to the Numberworks), never the Launchpad finale: the Garden Gate is a review door a learner walks to, not a start. (Before Launchpad opened, every such run started at Explorer 0.1 with the gap flagged on the Starting Point note; those stored rows are left exactly where they are, and the note says so.) Phase 2 (2026-11-05): the Unit 5-7 profiles were locked with the units themselves; before they shipped, a run meeting every Phase 1 profile landed at Explorer 5.1 as a named-but-unbuilt door, which is why older placement rows can carry that node - it is a real, built door now.
crosswalk.softLanding: If the learner then fails the first two checks at the placed start, the path quietly offers the previous unit first. Teacher/parent override is absolute and bypasses this table entirely.

rungConvention.half: X.5 = grade X's first clusters are secure; the staircase is sampling the second half of grade X.
rungConvention.whole: X.0 = the end of grade X-1 is secure; the staircase is sampling the start of grade X. (K.0 = the start of kindergarten.)

Algebra & Patterns.ccssThread: OA (K-5) -> RP (6-7, deferred) -> EE (6-8, deferred). Owns: operation meanings as algebra, properties, equations and unknowns, patterns, then ratios and expressions.

deferredRungs.6.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: ratio concepts begin (6.RP.A heading). Not taggable until the Pro lock.
deferredRungs.6.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: one-variable equations and inequalities (6.EE.B heading).
deferredRungs.7.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: proportional relationships (7.RP.A heading).
deferredRungs.7.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: equivalent expressions and multi-step equations (7.EE.A/B headings).
deferredRungs.8.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: linear equations and the bridge to functions (8.EE.B/C, 8.F.A/B headings; Number Quest bridges 8.F, never claims it).

1.0.focus: Addition/subtraction word problems within 20; properties used informally (e.g. swapping addends).

1.5.focus: The equals sign means 'the same as'; find the unknown in an equation; fluency building within 10/20.

2.0.focus: One- and two-step addition/subtraction problems within 100.

2.5.focus: Equal groups and arrays: the honest foundation of multiplication.

3.0.focus: What multiplication and division mean; properties as strategies; division as unknown-factor.

3.5.focus: Two-step problems with the four operations; arithmetic patterns explained (3.OA.D.8/9 - patterns live in OA.D at grade 3, not OA.C).

4.0.focus: Multistep problems including multiplicative comparison; factors, multiples, prime/composite.

4.5.focus: Generate and analyze a pattern from a rule; first numerical expressions with grouping symbols.

5.0.focus: Write and interpret expressions; two related patterns side by side.

5.5.focus: Paired patterns as ordered pairs, ready for the coordinate plane and for grade 6 expressions (6.EE lock deferred).

K.0.focus: Joining and taking apart within 5, with objects and drawings.

K.5.focus: Joining/taking apart within 10; make 10 from a smaller number; decompose to 10.

Data & Chance.ccssThread: MD data clusters (K-5: K.MD.B -> 1.MD.C -> 2.MD.D -> 3-5.MD.B) -> SP (6-8, deferred). Owns: sorting/counting, graphs, line plots, then statistical variability and (grade 7) probability.

deferredRungs.6.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: statistical variability and distributions (6.SP.A/B headings).
deferredRungs.6.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: summarizing distributions; chance still pre-standard at grade 6 (probability is 7.SP.C).
deferredRungs.7.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: random sampling and inference (7.SP.A/B headings).
deferredRungs.7.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: probability models (7.SP.C heading) - the first rung where chance items may carry a real code.
deferredRungs.8.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: bivariate data (8.SP.A heading; the full course marks it builds-toward/partial, spec section 2.5 note 9).

1.0.focus: Organize, represent and interpret data with up to three categories.

1.5.focus: Ask and answer how-many-more / how-many-fewer questions about a chart.

2.0.focus: Picture graphs and bar graphs (single-unit scale) to solve put-together / take-apart / compare problems.

2.5.focus: Line plots of whole-number measurements; bar graphs with scaled intervals beginning.

3.0.focus: Scaled picture and bar graphs; solve one- and two-step comparisons from a graph.

3.5.focus: Generate measurement data and show it on a line plot (halves and quarters of a unit).

4.5.focus: Add and subtract fractions using the data on a line plot.

5.0.focus: Line plots with fractional measurements (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) and operations on that data.

5.5.enrichment: Chance LANGUAGE only (impossible / unlikely / likely / certain, fair-game talk) may be sampled here as flagged enrichment. It carries NO code: no probability standard exists before grade 6 (spec section 2.1).
5.5.focus: Data fluency at end-of-Explorer depth; readiness for statistical variability in grade 6 (lock deferred).

K.0.focus: Classify objects into categories and count each category.

K.5.focus: Sort a category another way and compare the counts.

Number.ccssThread: CC (K) -> NBT (K-5) with OA operations woven in -> NF (3-5) -> NS (6-8, deferred). Owns: counting, place value, the four operations, fractions, then rationals.

deferredRungs.6.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: dividing fractions by fractions and rational numbers on the line (6.NS.A/C headings). Not taggable until the Pro lock.
deferredRungs.6.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: fluent multi-digit and decimal computation, common factors (6.NS.B heading).
deferredRungs.7.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: four operations with rational numbers (7.NS.A heading).
deferredRungs.7.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: rational-number fluency applied in expressions/equations (7.NS.A with 7.EE).
deferredRungs.8.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: irrational numbers approximated by rationals (8.NS.A heading; the full course marks it builds-toward, spec section 2.5 note 7).

1.0.focus: Count to 120 from any starting number; tens and ones; compare two-digit numbers.

1.5.focus: Add/subtract within 100 using place value (no regrouping into fluency); add and subtract within 20.

2.0.focus: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, 100s; hundreds/tens/ones; compare three-digit numbers.

2.5.focus: Add and subtract within 1000 with strategies; fluent (from memory) within 20.

3.0.focus: Round to 10/100; add/subtract within 1000; multiplication and division meanings within 100.

3.5.focus: Fractions as numbers, on the number line; fluent multiplication/division within 100.

4.0.focus: Place value generalised (ten-times rule); fluent multi-digit add/subtract; multi-digit multiplication and division with remainders.

4.5.focus: Fraction equivalence and ordering; build fractions from unit fractions (like-denominator add/subtract); decimal notation tenths/hundredths.

5.0.focus: The place-value system including decimals; operations with decimals to hundredths.

5.5.focus: Add/subtract unlike denominators; multiply and divide fractions in context - the bridge into grade 6 NS (lock deferred).

K.0.focus: Count sequence to 20 and beyond by ones; count objects to tell how many (cardinality).

K.5.focus: Count out a given number to 20; compare numbers to 10; compose/decompose 11-19 as ten ones and more.

Shape & Measure.ccssThread: G (K-8, continuous) + MD measurement clusters (K-5) -> G/SP measurement in 6-8 (deferred). Owns: shapes and their properties, length/time/money, area/perimeter, angles, volume, coordinates.

deferredRungs.6.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: area, surface area and volume of polygons and prisms (6.G.A heading).
deferredRungs.6.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: coordinate-plane polygons and nets (6.G.A heading).
deferredRungs.7.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: scale drawings and constructed figures (7.G.A heading).
deferredRungs.7.5: DEFERRED - orientation only: angle measure, area, surface area and volume incl. circles (7.G.B heading).
deferredRungs.8.0: DEFERRED - orientation only: congruence/similarity, Pythagoras, cylinders/cones/spheres (8.G.A/B/C headings).

1.0.focus: Order and compare lengths; measure by iterating a unit; shapes defined by their attributes.

1.5.focus: Tell time to the hour and half-hour; compose 2-D/3-D shapes; halves and fourths of shapes.

2.0.focus: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units; draw shapes with given attributes; thirds join halves/fourths.

2.5.focus: Length problems as addition/subtraction on the number line; time to five minutes; money values and problems (money's CCSS home starts at grade 2 - spec section 2.1).

3.0.focus: Elapsed time to the minute; liquid volumes and masses (metric); quadrilaterals and shape categories; partitioned shapes as unit fractions.

3.5.focus: Area as counting unit squares, tied to multiplication; perimeter of polygons, area/perimeter contrast.

4.0.focus: Measurement conversions (larger to smaller unit); points, lines, rays, angles drawn and identified; classify figures; symmetry.

4.5.focus: Angle concepts and measuring angles in degrees with a protractor.

5.0.focus: Convert like units within a system; the coordinate plane (axes, ordered pairs, first-quadrant graphing).

5.5.focus: Volume by unit cubes and by formula, related to multiplication; classify 2-D figures in a hierarchy.

K.0.focus: Describe and directly compare measurable attributes (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter); name shapes in any orientation.

K.5.focus: Compose bigger shapes from smaller ones; model and draw shapes; sorting by attribute (shared with Data & Chance K.0/K.5 by design - a sort item may serve either staircase, tagged to the strand that served it).
